answer.label: A misquotation rejected by
answer.sourceLine: Le Guin objected to this pseudo-quote on her own website. QI’s first known match is Robin W. Winks’s 1983 travel guide, possibly paraphrasing her earlier essay; neither his authorship nor the exact route is certain.

author.name: Ursula K. Le Guin
author.heading: About Ursula K. Le Guin
author.bio: Ursula K. Le Guin wrote speculative fiction that used imagined societies to examine power, gender and the ways people live together. Her books include A Wizard of Earthsea, The Left Hand of Darkness and The Dispossessed; her essays also defended imagination as an adult responsibility.

misattribution.truthLine: Do not copy this as a Le Guin quotation; Winks is an early documented transmitter, not a proven originator.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: A literary T-shirt request led Le Guin to investigate the words attributed to her. Her objection was substantive as well as bibliographic: she valued children’s imagination, but disliked the suggestion that growing up means losing the capacity to create.

schema.claimReviewed: Ursula K. Le Guin wrote “The creative adult is a child who has survived.”
schema.faqAnswer: No. Le Guin rejected this pseudo-quotation. QI finds an early appearance in Robin W. Winks’s 1983 book, but its exact creator is uncertain.
schema.verdictNote: Le Guin is the author whose credit is rejected, not the creator of this sentence.
